statement: Intel's EMIB-T advanced packaging yield has reportedly climbed above 90%, targeting mass production in 2027 at roughly half the cost of TSMC's CoWoS, with no primary announcement from Intel or MediaTek confirming it.
why: Advanced packaging is the binding constraint on AI accelerator output, so a credible second high-yield packaging path at materially lower cost would loosen the tightest link in the chain — but every order-specific claim here is trade-press attribution.

impact.mechanism: A second qualified 2.5D packaging route at high yield adds capacity outside TSMC CoWoS, easing the packaging bottleneck that currently gates accelerator shipments.

evidence.source: TechSoda 'Global Market Watch: Advanced Packaging Takes the Stage' (Substack)
evidence.excerpt: 'Intel's EMIB-T advanced packaging yield has reportedly climbed above 90%, targeting mass production in 2027 at roughly half the cost of TSMC's CoWoS.'

evidence.source: TechSoda 'Global Market Watch: Advanced Packaging Takes the Stage' (Substack)
evidence.excerpt: PRIMARY-SOURCE STATUS: NO primary announcement exists.

confidence.basis: Secondary trade-press only, hedged with 'reportedly', no primary announcement, and the originating lead itself contains a contradicting claim that a 50% substrate yield remains the bottleneck.

dispersion: The same originating lead says yields 'exceed 90%' while 'another report says a 50% substrate yield remains the bottleneck'.
